news.headline: Claude Code v2.1.319 changes auto mode behind gateways and adds a deny-instead-of-prompt setting for unattended runs
news.verdict: The most important release for anyone running Claude Code without a person watching: auto mode now refuses unchecked calls behind gateways, and a new setting stops runs waiting on prompts.
points: With telemetry or feature flags off, including behind LLM gateways, calls the server cannot check are now asked about or denied.
New permissions.denyInsteadOfPrompting denies a tool call that would wait on a prompt, and the turn continues.
claude -p now exits 1, not 0, when auto mode refused actions because no safety check was available.

image.alt: Claude Code v2.1.319 changes auto mode behind gateways and adds a deny-instead-of-prompt setting for unattended runs

news.headline: Claude Enterprise lets admins tag projects with cost codes and see spend by tag (beta)
news.verdict: Useful for firms that bill AI use back to clients or departments, but the exclusions mean many UK and regulated tenants cannot use it yet.
points: Projects can carry codes the organisation already uses, such as a charge code or client-matter number.
Not available with HIPAA configuration, customer-managed keys, zero data retention, or data stored outside the US.
Tags only work inside projects; work outside a project gets no tag.

image.alt: Claude Enterprise lets admins tag projects with cost codes and see spend by tag (beta)

news.headline: Perplexity launches Teammates, long-running work agents, plus a fully local Computer mode on Mac
points: Teammates take an ongoing job, plan it, run tasks in parallel and follow through; first on web for Max subscribers.
Each teammate runs in a separate environment, with browser sessions kept apart from other teammates.
Fully local Computer on Mac: Pro, Max and Enterprise, app 26.42.0 or later, 36 GB unified memory recommended.

image.alt: Perplexity launches Teammates, long-running work agents, plus a fully local Computer mode on Mac

news.headline: DigitalOcean launches Cuttlefish, an iPhone app to watch and approve agent runs on its Managed Agents
points: Native iPhone app to follow live agent sessions, approve or deny tool calls, and steer or stop a run.
Works with Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode, OpenHands, Hermes, LangGraph and CrewAI on Managed Agents.
Managed Agents is a public preview; Box Mount for Managed Agents is a private preview.

image.alt: DigitalOcean launches Cuttlefish, an iPhone app to watch and approve agent runs on its Managed Agents

news.headline: Cursor adds realtime voice calls with its coding agents, running on Grok Voice
news.verdict: Voice supervision of coding agents is now a shipping feature in a major editor, and it relies on xAI as a supplier.
points: Users can talk with agents in a realtime voice call: describe a change, ask for status, hear progress.
Works in the Agents Window, the IDE, on web and in Cursor for iOS.
Runs on Grok Voice; with Privacy Mode on, voice chat runs with zero data retention.

image.alt: Cursor adds realtime voice calls with its coding agents, running on Grok Voice

news.headline: @GitHub in Slack and Teams is generally available: chat conversations can turn into issues and pull requests
news.verdict: Chat-to-pull-request is now a supported product inside Teams, which is where most UK enterprise clients already work.
points: Investigate bugs, create issues, implement changes and open pull requests without leaving the conversation.
Canvas shows plans, code changes and previews beside the conversation.
Issues and pull requests made by @GitHub now record which Slack or Teams conversation and user created them.

image.alt: @GitHub in Slack and Teams is generally available: chat conversations can turn into issues and pull requests

news.headline: Copilot code review settings can now be managed by API, and comments show which skills and MCP servers they used
news.verdict: AI review is getting the controls enterprises need: policy as code, source attribution per comment and cost per review.
points: Copilot code review settings are manageable through REST and GraphQL, from enterprise policy down to repositories.
Each comment can show which skills, MCP servers and custom instructions Copilot reported as sources.
Code review agent sessions now show the AI credits a review consumed.

image.alt: Copilot code review settings can now be managed by API, and comments show which skills and MCP servers they used

news.headline: Microsoft runs Qwen3.8-27B locally through Foundry Local and connects it to GitHub Copilot
news.verdict: A credible fully local coding-agent option now exists for clients who cannot send code to a cloud model, at consumer GPU cost.
points: With 4-bit quantisation the model is about 18 GB and runs on consumer GPUs with 24 GB of VRAM.
Microsoft reports higher generation speed at every tested prompt length, widening beyond 131K tokens.
Needs Foundry Local CLI 0.13.0 or later; Macs and AMD GPUs are on the roadmap.

image.alt: Microsoft runs Qwen3.8-27B locally through Foundry Local and connects it to GitHub Copilot

news.headline: OpenAI brings in Hacktron to test how its systems connect to third-party services
news.verdict: The labs now treat the joins between agents and outside services as the main attack surface, which is where client agent projects carry most risk too.
points: Hacktron and OpenAI engineers will test high-priority areas, focused on how OpenAI's systems interact with third-party services.
Hacktron gets wider access to OpenAI's frontier models through Daybreak Red.
OpenAI met Hacktron through its bug bounty, and recently raised bounty rewards.

news.headline: Censys finds about 815 exposed deployments of the Artex AI attack console
news.verdict: Autonomous attack tooling is now common enough to scan for at internet scale; client security briefings should assume AI-driven probing.
points: Censys counted 1,465 hosts with exposed consoles, about 815 distinct deployments after de-duplication.
155 hosts also ran other attack frameworks such as Cobalt Strike or Vshell.
Hunting tips: default ports 8787 and 8790, and unfamiliar LLM proxies such as CLIProxyAPI in egress logs.

image.alt: Censys finds about 815 exposed deployments of the Artex AI attack console

news.headline: Microsoft starts fair-use limits on Copilot Chat for unlicensed users; large organisations from 9 November
news.verdict: Free Copilot Chat inside Microsoft 365 is getting usage caps, which will push heavier users at clients towards paid seats or alternatives.
points: Limits started 2 November for organisations with 2,000 or fewer Microsoft 365 seats.
Larger organisations get the limits from 9 November 2026.
Microsoft does not publish the limits; admins cannot view or adjust them, and no admin action is required.

image.alt: Microsoft starts fair-use limits on Copilot Chat for unlicensed users; large organisations from 9 November

news.headline: Cloudflare AI Gateway now flags provider keys that have not been used for 90 days
news.verdict: A small but useful control: unused AI provider keys are risk without value, and gateways are starting to point them out.
points: A new Key security section highlights keys whose recorded activity is older than 90 days.
Usage tracking starts November 2026, so older inactivity is not yet visible.
It applies to provider keys stored in AI Gateway.

image.alt: Cloudflare AI Gateway now flags provider keys that have not been used for 90 days
